a.description: array from which to take values.

indices.description: N-dimensional array of integer indices of values to take from the array.

axis.description: the axis along which to take values. If not specified, the array will be flattened before indexing is applied.

mode.description: Out-of-bounds indexing mode, either ``"fill"`` or ``"clip"``. The default ``mode="fill"`` returns invalid values (e.g. NaN) for out-of bounds indices; the ``fill_value`` argument gives control over this value. For more discussion of ``mode`` options, see :attr:`jax.numpy.ndarray.at`.
constraints: mode must be one of fill, clip, jax.numpy.ndarray.at

unique_indices.description: If True, the implementation will assume that the indices are unique after normalization of negative indices, which lets the compiler emit more efficient code during the backward pass. If set to True and normalized indices are not unique, the result is implementation-defined and may be non-deterministic.

indices_are_sorted.description: If True, the implementation will assume that the indices are sorted in ascending order after normalization of negative indices, which can lead to more efficient execution on some backends. If set to True and normalized indices are not sorted, the output is implementation-defined.

fill_value.description: The fill value to return for out-of-bounds slices when mode is 'fill'. Ignored otherwise. Defaults to NaN for inexact types, the largest negative value for signed types, the largest positive value for unsigned types, and True for booleans.
constraints: fill_value must be one of fill
